newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady under RBI's watchful eye.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady under RBI's watchful eye.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady against the dollar at 35.8150/8250 on Friday, dealers said.
They said RBI's dominant presence in the market held the rupee even without its actual intervention.
"They only made enquiries today," said a dealer referring to RBI's dollar purchases at the 35.82 level on Thursday.
RBI had passively bought at the 35.82 level during the week with no questions asked, a dealer said.
It no longer seemed to be intervening reluctantly as wit had until the first week of June.
"Possibly passive intervention kills the traders' instinct to speculate while aggressive intervention enhances the killer instinct," Societe Generale Bank said in a forex commentary.
No major dollar demand is expected in the middle of the month and with the oil price hike in limbo, there appeared to be no market-moving event on the horizon, dealers said.
Nor do banks expect any immediate impact from government's initiatives to promote capital outflows in a bid to use up the foreign exchange inflows into the country.
"We can look forward to the stalemate continuing next week," a dealer said.
The forward premiums continued soft as exporters continued selling pressure with few takers.
The six month annualised forward premium closed steady at 4.07 percent.
"There is a lot of scepticism whether it will come down further," said a dealer.
